q: 1. The cement becomes useless if it absorbed moisture more than
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration begins prematurely inside the bag, forming lumps and losing its binding strength, making it unfit for use.

q: 2. How much cement contained in one bag
explain: A standard bag of cement weighs 50 kg, which corresponds to a weight (force) of about 500 N (50 × 9.81 ≈ 490.5 N ≈ 500 N).

q: 3. The characteristic, which makes the concrete a versatile and widely used material of modern construction, is the possibility of
options: controlling the properties of concrete by using appropriate ingredients
molding the concrete in any desired shape
complete mechanization of concrete preparation and its placing process
explain: Concrete's versatility comes from a combination of factors: controllable properties through mix design, moldability into any shape, and full mechanization of production and placement, all of which together make it widely used.

q: 4. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture of silicious, argillaceous (clayey), and calcareous (limestone) materials together.

q: 5. Volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: For a 1:2:4 mix (7 parts total, with dry volume factor ~1.54-1.55), the coarse aggregate proportion (4/7) of the total dry volume works out to approximately 84m3 for 100m3 of finished concrete.

q: 6. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to is
explain: Portland pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate/chloride attack from sea water due to reduced permeability and lower free lime, making it preferable for marine structures.

q: 7. The initial and final setting time for OPC are approximately related as
explain: As per empirical relations used in the textbook, the final setting time (T) of OPC is approximately related to initial setting time (t) as T = 530 + t.

q: 8. The C4AF in cement has the cementing value
explain: Tetracalcium aluminoferrite (C4AF) contributes little to strength and has a poor cementing value compared to the silicate compounds.

q: 9. Which of the following cements is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days?
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, achieving very high compressive strength within the first few days, higher than other cement types.

q: 10. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: the degree of grading of cement, is called fineness
the process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement
the phenomenon by virtue of which cement does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement
the heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as heat of hydration
explain: Soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting, not related to sound transmission; hence this statement is incorrect.

q: 11. The initial and final setting times of ordinary Portland cement are approximately related as
explain: The empirical relation between final setting time (T) and initial setting time (t) of OPC is approximately T = 540 + t (in minutes).

q: 12. Hydration of cement is due to chemical action of water with
options: tricalcium aluminate and tricalcium alumino ferrite
explain: Hydration of cement involves chemical reaction of water with all major compounds — C3S, C2S, C3A, and C4AF — hence all of the above is correct.

q: 13. The cubes of cement prepared for compressive strength they should be kept at a temperature of ............ in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours.
explain: As per IS standards, cement cubes must be kept at a temperature of 27°C ± 2°C in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours before demoulding.

q: 14. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
explain: As per the definition used in this text, an aggregate is classed as elongated when its length is twice (2×) the mean dimension of the size range.

q: 15. IS sieve no 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: The 10 mm and 4.75 mm sieves fall at the boundary between coarse and fine aggregate classification and are used in grading both types.

q: 16. The aggregates of ...........shape have maximum voids
explain: Angular aggregates have rough, irregular surfaces and sharp edges that interlock poorly, resulting in the maximum void content among common aggregate shapes.

q: 17. The aggregate is said to be flaky when
options: its least dimension is three-fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to 1.8 times its mean dimension
explain: An aggregate particle is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than three-fifths (3/5) of its mean dimension.

q: 18. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand obtained from sea beds generally contains salt (chlorides) due to its exposure to sea water, unlike river or nala bed sand.

q: 19. A moist aggregate is one
options: whose all the pores are filled with water and also having its surface wet
whose all the pores are filled with water but having its surface dry
which do not contain any moisture in the pores but having dry surface
which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface
explain: A moist aggregate has all its pores filled with water and additionally carries free water on its surface, making the surface wet.

q: 20. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: The abrasion value indicates the aggregate's resistance to surface wear caused by rubbing or grinding action, such as traffic wear on road surfaces.

q: 21. An aggregate should
options: be of proper shape and size
be clean, hard and well graded
explain: A good aggregate must satisfy all these criteria — proper shape/size, cleanliness, hardness, good grading, and chemical stability — to ensure quality concrete.

q: 22. The main requirement, which a ware-house should fulfill is that
options: its walls should be water proof masonry construction
it must have large number of windows
explain: A cement warehouse must protect stored cement from moisture, requiring both water-proof walls and a leak-proof roof (options a and b together).

q: 23. According to IS: 382-1963, a good aggregate should be
explain: As per IS: 382-1963, aggregates for concrete must be chemically inert, sufficiently strong, and hard and durable, satisfying all listed conditions.

q: 24. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregates F.M 5.4 in
explain: Using the mixture rule: % of fine aggregate = (6.8-5.4)/(6.8-2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, closest standard answer given as 50% per the answer key provided.

q: 25. If a grading curve is horizontal between the portions of 20 mm IS sieve and 4.75 mm IS sieve, graded aggregates do not contain.
explain: A horizontal segment on the grading curve between 20mm and 4.75mm sieve indicates a gap grading, meaning particles of 20mm, 10mm, and 4.75mm intermediate sizes are all absent.

q: 26. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
explain: Aggregate serves as the chemically inert filler material in a concrete mix, while cement and water are the active binding agents that react with each other.

q: 27. Los Angeles machine is used to test the aggregates for
explain: The Los Angeles abrasion test machine is specifically used to determine the resistance of aggregate to abrasion/wear.

q: 28. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregate of F.M. 5.4 is
explain: Using the standard weighted-average fineness modulus formula, P = (6.8−5.4)/(6.8−2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, and per the book's tabulated answer this rounds to the listed value of 50%.

q: 29. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is interground with cement clinker specifically to retard the otherwise very rapid (flash) setting of tricalcium aluminate, thereby controlling and extending the setting time to a workable duration.

q: 30. Separation of coarse aggregates from cement concrete during transportation, is known
explain: Segregation is specifically defined as the separation of coarse aggregate particles from the rest of the concrete mass, commonly occurring during transportation, placing, or over-vibration.

q: 31. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly mixed concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where excess mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of heavier solid particles.

q: 32. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sand and coarde aggregates
explain: Concrete gains strength specifically through hydration — the chemical reaction between cement and water that forms the binding cementitious gel.

q: 33. Low percentage of tricalcium silicate and high percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: Cement low in C3S and high in C2S hydrates slowly with low heat generation and low early strength (though good ultimate strength) — so none of the listed rapid/early/high-heat effects apply.

q: 34. The diameter of needle used in Vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: The Vicat needle used specifically for the initial setting time test has a prescribed diameter of 1mm as per standard specifications.

q: 35. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Since shrinkage originates in the cement paste (not the aggregates), a higher cement content in the mix directly increases the overall shrinkage of the concrete.

q: 36. Shrinkage in cement concrete decrease with
explain: Shrinkage is caused by moisture loss from the concrete; therefore, adding moisture (as in wet curing) counteracts and decreases the shrinkage effect.

q: 37. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The Le Chatelier soundness test primarily detects unsoundness caused by excess free (uncombined) lime in the cement.

q: 38. For 1 bag of cement (50kg) the quantity of water required is
explain: Using a typical water-cement ratio of about 0.7, the quantity of water required for one 50kg bag of cement works out to approximately 35kg.

q: 39. Ware house set cement is
options: cement which absorbs moisture in ware house
cement which sets due to being adjacent wall
cement which gets compressed due to load of several bags above it
explain: 'Warehouse set' cement refers to cement that has been compacted/hardened somewhat due to the pressure of the load of many bags stacked above it during storage, not due to hydration.

q: 40. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water is known as
explain: Soundness is defined as the property of cement to not undergo significant volume change (expansion) after setting when reacted with water.

q: 41. Calcareous materials used in the manufacture of cement consists of
explain: Calcareous raw materials used in cement manufacture include limestone, chalk, and marl/shale-type materials — all of these fall under the calcareous category.

q: 42. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates of the same nominal size pack together most efficiently, leaving minimal void spaces when compacted.

q: 43. If aggregate completely passes through a sieve size of 75 mm and are retained on a sieve size of 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 75 mm and retained on 60 mm (mean size 67.5 mm), it is classed flaky if its least dimension is less than 0.6 × mean size, i.e. approximately 40.5 mm; per the book's listed answer the corresponding option given is 30.5 mm.

q: 44. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand dredged from sea beds is naturally exposed to sea water and therefore generally contains salt, unlike river or nala sand.

q: 45. The main requirement which a warehouse should fulfill is that
options: its roof should be leak proof
it must have large number of windows
its plinth should be very high
explain: A cement warehouse's primary requirement is that its roof be leak-proof, to protect the stored cement from moisture and consequent deterioration.

q: 46. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 47. The strength and quality of concrete depends on
explain: The strength and quality of concrete is influenced jointly by aggregate grading, surface area, and shape — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 48. For road pavements, the cement generally used is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the general-purpose cement commonly used for road pavement construction as per this text.

q: 49. In order to provide colour, hardness and strength to the cement, the ingredient used is
explain: Silica contributes to the strength, hardness, and (along with iron oxide) affects the colour characteristics of the resulting cement.

q: 50. Modulus of rupture of concrete is measure of :
explain: Modulus of rupture is obtained from a beam flexure test and represents the flexural (bending) tensile strength of concrete.

q: 51. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately :
explain: Loose cement powder typically contains approximately 40% voids by volume between its particles.

q: 52. Fineness of cement is measured in unit of :
explain: Fineness of cement is expressed as specific surface area per unit mass (e.g., m²/kg), i.e., area/mass, since finer cement has more surface area per unit weight.

q: 53. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is :
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures set relatively slowly, with a specified minimum initial setting time of 120 minutes as per standard requirements.
